Vala's (Claudia Black) father Jacek (guest star Fred Willard) contacts Stargate Command wishing to trade information about a series of planned attacks on Earth in exchange for sanctuary on the planet. Also starring Ben Browder and Michael Shanks.

In an elaborate plan using Vala Mal Doran (Claudia Black) as bait to capture Adria (guest star Morena Baccarin), SG-1 themselves are surprised when Ba'al (guest star Cliff Simon) intercepts Adria from under them to use in his own evil plan.

The team races to foil the Goa'uld's plans to destroy Atlantis after Maj. Gen. Landry informs them that a bomb has been planted, triggered to detonate the next time the team heads to Earth. Meanwhile, two Wraith ships are heading towards Atlantis.

While testing a newly repaired puddle jumper, McKay and Captain Hugh Griffin suddenly lose control of the ship and crash into the ocean. As the jumper begins to sink slowly towards the bottom of the ocean, Griffin sacrifices himself to save McKay.

Sheppard and the team discover a world that has technology created by the Ancients. But the planet's royal family does not allow anyone but them to harness the technology and treat the villagers with little dignity.

The team discover two life pods floating in space. Upon further investigation, the team accidentally transfers the minds of the individuals into Sheppard and Weir. Things get worse when the team discovers the two people are out to destroy the other.

With extinction imminent, the Asgard hand over all their knowledge and technology to SG-1, but not before the Ori launch an attack trying to intercede. Starring Ben Browder, Amanda Tapping, Christopher Judge, Beau Bridges, and Michael Shanks.

When the SG-1 crew discovers that a final assault on Earth is in the works and a double-agent is scheming among them, their mission takes on a new meaning as they travel to the Ori's home galaxy to overtake their arch enemy before it's too late.

As Colonel Jack O'Neill and his team journey to Abydos to confront deadly warriors and laser-firing Death Gliders, O'Neill realizes that this new mission seems hauntingly familiar and that an old enemy has returned to take his revenge on Earth.

Col. Sheppard's team is urgently summoned to M1K-177, where Maj. Lorne's team has been attacked. When Sheppard and his unit arrive, however, all they find is a burned building containing charred bodies: presumably, Lorne and his men.

Lt. Kenmore wakes up in the infirmary without his memory. He begins to think there is something wrong when his nightmares about being a Wraith seem to be more than real. His fears would be unfounded if not for the serum that turns Wraiths humans.

Sheppard and the team visits the planet Taranis at the invitation of two leading citizens, Dr. Norina Pero and Chancellor Lycus, who want McKay to repair a failing shield generator at an Ancient base, and Ancient warship, they've discovered.

Kenmore arrives back in Atlantis with a group of Wraith, in the midst of a civil war. Kenmore, hoping to leverage his knowledge of Atlantis against Sheppard and the team, suggests a trade; Beckett's serum, in exchange for keeping Atlantis hidden.

A letter from beyond the grave brings new hope and life to an estranged family.
The postal detectives are faced with a challenge when a letter from the futures turns up.
When Celeste loses her teaching job, she becomes an au pair for an infamous New York property tycoon.

Lexi has two weeks before she takes her rightful place as a royal princess. She must reveal her true identity to her best friend and find a suitable date for the royal gala, all under the watchful eye of her handsome, but infuriating, bodyguard Noah.
Georgie's graduation has finally arrived but so has a mysterious figure from her past.
Amy is asked to spend time at an art retreat to work with an artist's allegedly traumatized horse.

Hoping to boost her career, a celebrity agrees to go on a reality TV show to marry her perfect match, a man she's never met. She soon tries to track him down to clarify that the marriage is just for show.

On the brink of divorce, James and Michelle have drifted apart over the years. They wake up to discover they have somehow switched bodies. Unable to switch back, they are forced to understand what the other goes through on a daily basis.
Tim is organizing an important rodeo when an old flame blows back into Hudson asking for his help.
Amy and Ty get some unexpected news about Luke just as Amy has to face an upsetting truth about Spartan.
Rehearsals begin for two choirs, one from rural New Zealand and one from New York City; they start on a joyful journey to the World Choir Games, the largest choral competition on Earth.
The World Choir Games are just weeks away; the rehearsal schedule is grueling, maybe too grueling, as exhaustion takes a toll.
When fears of holding on or letting go grip the family, they look to each other for support through dangerous challenges.

The past year has brought unexpected change to the Heartland family; Amy deals with a major upheaval in her life; Lou copes with the reality of being the mayor of Hudson; Georgie revisits her dream of the Olympics.

Amy must face a difficult truth when her efforts to help a young girl form a connection with her new horse takes an unexpected turn; Lou faces harsh criticism as mayor; a cattle drive brings up difficult memories for Jack.
(S06E008) Dave turns to the Heidi in hopes of forming an alliance.

(S06E001) Faced with the constant threat of flooding and exhaustive heat, not to mention the flesh-eating piranhas, new rules are introduced for the sixth installment of TV's most popular reality series.
(S06E002) The discovery of hidden food threatens to send one tribe over the edge.
(S06E003) The women elect a team leader who has no desire to be put in that position.
(S06E004) A tribe member, who seemingly has no allies, rethinks strategy.
(S06E005) Just when the tribes begin to settle in their environment, a surprise tempts the existing alliances within the tribes.
(S06E006) One castaway forms an alliance with a hated tribe member whom they fully intend to betray.
(S06E007) With the ousting of Roger, Dave acknowledges that he’s on thin ice with the tribe and realizes he needs to form a new strategy to stay.

A woman questions Alex's courage; he becomes a daredevil and has an exciting ski-trip; he decides to live life to the fullest from then on and signs up for skydiving for the first time.

In a hilarious caper, Louie and the cabbies pool all their cash to buy a painting at an auction, planning to cash in big when the artist dies—but when the bidding gets too heavy, the gang turns a dignified auction into a frolicking free-for-all.
The cabbies conjure up their own outrageous fantasies when Herve Villechaize of Fantasy Island leaves an envelope in Tony's cab.
The cabbies continue to fantasize while waiting for Herve Villechaize of Fantasy Island to pick up his envelope.
Latka blows his life's savings on a luxurious penthouse when his apartment is demolished.
Alex's romantic affair with a television soap actress leads to thoughts of matrimony.
Latka decides to return to his native country to fight in a revolution.

Elaine suddenly starts getting mysterious love letters. When she becomes intrigued by the poetic propositions, a couple of cabbies quickly claim responsibility, leaving Elaine with the hilarious task of discovering who is the amorous writer.
Louie makes a horrible first impression on girlfriend Zena’s parents on Taxi. Louie’s romance with girlfriend Zena takes an outrageous twist when she brings him home to meet her parents.

It’s a hilarious shock to the cabbies when Rev. Jim brings his new pet to the garage—an over-the-hill racehorse that he bought after cashing in on the 300-to-1 long shot. However, he soon finds that it’s impossible to housebreak a horse.
It’s a dream come true for Tony when he’s challenged by an aging ex-champ, but he has more than just a fight on his hand when the opposition unveils its secret weapon.
The cabbies try to make Tony a family man when they convince him to adopt the adorably precocious eight-year-old boy named Brian whom he befriended.
Romantic sparks fly when Latka meets Simka Dahblitz, who is from his native country.

Bobby faces a humorous predicament when it becomes obvious that one of the biggest talent managers in New York is representing him because of his prowess as a lover, and not for his ability as an actor.
In a protest against unsafe equipment, the cabbies go on strike, and Louie offers an unusual solution to the problem to shop steward Elaine.
Aunt Bee stirs up a crusade for a chicken farmer whose property has been condemned to make way for a new road.
Barney adds a vintage motorcycle to the rolling stock of the Mayberry Sheriff's department, to the Sheriff's regret.
Ernest T. Bass is a would-be Romeo, who is brought into the sheriff's home in an effort to teach him some manners.
A beautiful prisoner threatens to crumble the security of the Mayberry jail, as both Andy and Barney fall for her charms.
Otis Campbell acquires a car and threatens life and limb of Mayberry's pedestrian population.
Barney suffers an ego blow when Gomer out-sings him for a part in the Mayberry Choir. Andy Griffith's wife, Barbara, appears in this episode as a member of the singing group.
Barney disguises himself as a dummy in an attempt to solve a series of theft at the Mayberry department store.
Andy takes a week off, leaving Barney and Gomer in charge. A prisoner also takes off in the resultant confusion.
After Andy wakes up Gomer to put out a small fire at the filling station, Gomer dedicates himself to repaying Andy in return for saving his life.
Aunt Bee saves money by buying a side of beef. The beef is tough, the freezer conks out, and Gomer attempts to fix the motor.
A strange mountain-style divorce ritual is frustrated by another ritual performed by Barney.
When Opie gets caught in a scheme to sell a useless product, Barney and Gomer come to his rescue.
Joyce Jameson and Jean Carson appear as two fun-loving blondes who upset the sheriff's office.
British comedian Bernard Fox plays an Englishman who returns to Mayberry and upsets Aunt Bee with his efficiency.
Barney interprets a kiss as a sign of a secret engagement between Andy and Helen. The town gets the word and prepares a surprise party for the couple.
After the Clampetts accidentally run into a beatnik he moves into the Clampett mansion, but neither he nor they know what to make of each other.

As a favor to Jed Mr. Drysdale arranges for a playboy bank director (who normally only dates women half his age) to come court Granny, while Jed goes out with a beautiful woman who dates rich older men.

Granny wants Jed to find a wife and asks for Mr. Drysdale's help. He introduces Jed to Phyllis but learns too late she a gold digger and becomes alarmed when they head to the track. But it's Granny they need to worry about.
Jethro decides to become a double naught spy and converts the family's truck into his idea of a Bondmobile. But he becomes the unwitting pawn in another banker's scheme.
Mr. Drysdale's biggest rival John Cushing succeeds in getting the Clampetts to transfer all of their money to his bank.

Mrs. Drydale's poodle Claude is to enter a dog show but gets sick right before. Granny offers to doctor the dog but Ellie Mae is concerned he doesn't know any tricks so she decides to help out with one of her own pets.

John Brewster, the oilman from Tulsa, is bringing his new bride to California for their honeymoon. Somehow the Clampetts get the idea that their backyard rustic cabin is the ideal place for the Brewsters to stay.
With the arrival of spring, the Countess returns for Granny's new batch of spring tonic. Granny thinks she's looking for a new husband and that Jed is her perfect match.
Mr. Drysdale owns a building that houses a beatnik's club. He hopes to get rid of them when they can't pay their rent but they find a new a sponsor: Jed Clampett.
Jed soon regrets helping out the beatniks with their money problems when Jethro, Elly May (and even Granny!) decide to join them.
Mr. Drysdale is appalled to learn that Jed is going door-to-door peddling his services as a handyman. But then he's apoplectic when he discovers that Jed has been hired by a rival bank.
Jed gets an honorary doctorate when he donates money to the college that Mr. Drysdale attended. Now the family thinks he can now practice medicine, which doesn't sit well with Granny.

Mrs. Drysdale thinks she can get the hillbillies to move out by throwing herself at Jed. Meanwhile Granny is itching to fight her because she fell into the cement pond when Jed had to stop a fight between them earlier.
An old friend from back in the hills is now an Elvis like singing idol. The Clampetts misunderstand the situation and decide to help Johnny get on his feet.
Johnny Poke's mother arrives from the Ozarks and Granny's matchmaking begins. Jed and Emma Poke come up with a plan to discourage her.
One person makes closed-minded comments about a competitor's identity, the players endure an eating contest and race during Dine-n-Dash, and two women face off in the Ascender duel.
The men and women partner up in the Stacking Stairs challenge, two friends compete in the Pole Wrestle duel, and a player moves in for a highly anticipated first kiss.
The players go head-to-head in the Ice Breakers challenge, and one competitor is determined to step up her game as two women put their strength to the test in the Push Me duel.
The men and women team up for the difficult Sunken Treasure challenge, two guys go at it in the Ascender duel, and one player feels used by another competitor.
The competitors must collect flags as they circle a 40-foot truss in the Around the Block challenge, a player goes back on her word, and two women head to The Duel to play I Can.
The remaining players compete in Paddle Me, which guarantees two people a spot in the finals, and a double duel night of Push Me and I Can determines the other two contenders left standing.
The final four compete in a challenge called The Rio Deal, and the man and woman who come out on top walk away with $150,000 each.
Miss USA 2003 Susie Castillo sits down with cast members from The Duel to discuss big moments from the season, including fights, hookups and never-before-seen footage.
The cast members arrive in Cape Town, South Africa, and settle into their new digs. Later, things get ugly between CT and Davis.
Bad Asses square up against the Good Guys in the Latter Race challenge and the first elimination is set to go down in the Inferno.

The first male Inferno provides a much needed confidence boost for one of the teams. Tension rocks the Bad Asses team as they try to keep it together in the Battering Ram challenge. Two female competitors are targeted for elimination in the Inferno.
Susie hatches a devious plan to win the Life Shield. The teams perform a daring mid-air stunt at the Wrap 'N Roll challenge. A shocking elimination ends in an epic emotional outburst.
A night of partying turns ugly for the Good Guys. The Bad Asses worry about the stability of their fiery vocal leader, Danny. Strategy is the name of the game at the Rope Burn challenge.

Danny deals with the lingering effects of the death of his mother. The Bad Asses look to end the Good Guys' winning streak at the Reversible Climbing Wall challenge. A hotly contested Inferno leaves one disappointed player eliminated.

Tonya declares verbal warfare on Good Guy Susie. A controversial decision puts the Good Guys' success in jeopardy at the Grape Smash challenge. Two familiar females are nominated to face off in the Inferno.
Darlene earns a promotion at Wellman Plastics, while Ben decides on a new career path; Jackie tries an herbal tea. and it leads to an emotional revelation.
Chuck's new purchase of a boat creates a rift; Darlene hires her first assistant at Wellman's Plastics but soon realizes she is anything but helpful.
Darlene starts to feel the pressures of her new job; Dan attempts to help Ben out at the hardware store, but the two don't always agree on how to run the business.
Mark is convinced he has COVID-19; Becky and Harris team up to confront Josh, who has been 'ghosting' Harris.
Dan feels helpless when Louise refuses to let him put himself at risk for her; when Jackie learns the competing restaurants are posting negative reviews.
Becky meets up with an old friend and feels pressured to impress him; Dan questions his position at the hardware store, leading to a massive fight between him and Ben.
Becky is working double shifts and taking classes at the community college, resulting in less time with her daughter; Dan decides to foster an elderly dog.
Darlene learns some shocking news about an old friend; the Conners family comes together to help someone close to them.
Dan encounters a surprise visitor who shares some unsolicited advice, leaving him feeling guilty; Darlene welcomes a new employee to Wellman Plastics.
Mark is stressed and exhausted from studying for an important entrance exam, so Darlene steps in to help, but her plan backfires.

The tread of a tire, a single shoe print and even the shape of a bruise help investigators track down killers, based solely on their patterns of guilt.
Most victims of multiple murderers are meticulously chosen because of a mutual connection with the killer or because they match an intricate set of criteria that fits the killer's MO.
Psychological Profiling: Journey into the dark recesses and calculated madness present only in our worst nightmares and in the minds of serial killers.

A victim usually never foresees danger when the perpetrator turns out to be a friend or a lover. Science and microscopic evidence can unmask these killers and find justice for those who are Loved To Death.

At a crime scene, anything left behind or seemingly out of place is considered a clue. But a fire can extinguish everything in its path, challenging forensic investigators at every turn and making each arson a trial by fire.
Men don't have a monopoly on murder, but it's still extraordinary when women kill. Though female killers are as deadly as males, they choose less violent methods.

A southeastern Virginia community is stunned by a crime no one can believe. A pregnant woman murdered, her baby lost. Across the state, another town feels a similar shock, a brutal, random slaying in a most unexpected setting.

Toxicology: While drugs can cure disease and ease pain, they can also be agents of murder. Toxicologists can examine blood and tissue to uncover cases where death is not as natural as it may seemfrom slow arsenic poisoning to quick cocaine overdoses.

Drowning deaths often look like accidents and water can destroy the scant clues the killer may have left behind. Investigators must turn to forensic science to solve cases where the victim is found dead in the water.

Approximately 1.8 million Americans are reported missing each year. Some are runaways who find their way home, but others simply disappear. When foul play is suspected, investigators turn to forensics to find the missing.
There are several things that can suggest murder; jealousy, anger, poison! When everyday substances reveal hidden clues that break a homicide case, those substances become the elements of murder.
Drug trafficking has spawned a violent and deadly criminal underground. It's providing a challenge to forensic investigators devoted to cracking drug rings.
Ballistics: A corpse is found with a gunshot wound to the head; the weapon lies next to the victim. It looks like suicide, but could it be murder? It's a question best solved by ballistics experts.
When teenagers are driven to kill, their victims are but the first to fall. In three such cases, the families of the killers, as well as their communities, become the victims of violent crime.
DNA Analysis: With the advent of DNA analysis, just a few microscopic cells found at a crime scene can be used to put a murder behind bars.

Super Shredder teste un nouveau super mutagène concocté par Stockman-mouche, qui se révèle parfait pour sa prochaine mission : exterminer tous ses ennemis sans exception, et sans empathie.

Les tortues rendent visite à Karaï à l'hôpital. Elle leur révèle où se trouve la planque de Super Shredder. Il s'agit d'une forteresse high-tech en pleine forêt, défendue par ses footbots et autres sergents.
Les tortues enquêtent sur une mystérieuse secte qui se réunit dans les égoûts. Tiger Claw a décidé de ressusciter Super Shredder.
Tiger Claw ordonne à Kavaxas de ramener Rahzar à la vie, ce qu'il parvient à faire. Il lui dit de reproduire ce prodige avec Shredder. Mais il lui manque un élément essentiel, le Kuro Kabuto.
Kavaxas a besoin du cœur de Shredder pour le ressusciter. C'est Don Vizioso qui s'en est emparé et qui le conserve dans une fiole. Les tortues et Tiger Claw vont tout faire pour le lui reprendre.
Shredder prend le pouvoir et détruit le sceau. Kavaxas est libre, il ouvre le portail du Royaume des Ténèbres et les revenants déferlent sur Terre.
Maître Splinter réunit ses quatre fils, pas encore adolescents. Il leur raconte en détail la genèse de leur histoire, et leurs débuts dans les rues hostiles de New York.
Panique le soir d'Halloween : New York est envahi de vrais zombies, vampires et loups-garous. April et Casey sont contaminés.

Same as it Never Was: Ultimate Drako's time manipulations have sent Donatello to an alternate reality … and it's not pretty. It's one possible future, a horrible nightmare. The Shredder is all powerful.
The Real World - Part 1: Ultimate Drako is causing trouble with the Time Scepter. He blasts Leonardo into another dimension … Usagi Yojimbo's dimension.

The Real World - Part 2: Leonardo and Usagi arrive in the Battle Nexus hoping for a way to reunite the four turtles and their master. But, they find the Battle Nexus under the control of the evil Ultimate Drako. Master Splinter is his prisoner.

Bishop's Gambit: Bishop is back and making his move. His research demands a mutated specimen closer to human … a rat: Master Splinter. Bishop kidnaps Splinter and moves to finish the creation of his genetically enhanced super soldiers.

Exodus - Part 1: Splinter receives a vision of his Master Yoshi…and a mission. He must stop the Shredder.Time is running out. He doesn't know how to explain it to his sons, but they need no explanation.They're with their father to the bitter end.

Exodus - Part 2: The Shredder is leaving earth in spaceship of his own construction intent upon wreaking havoc on the Utroms and the galaxy. But, he's taken on some unwanted passengers and, they're not about to let the Shredder get away.

Cousin Sid: Casey and April bring the Turtles and Splinter to Casey's farmhouse to heal up from the beating they took in the final fight with the Shredder. But before they can start to recover, Casey's cousin Sid crashes the scene…

The People's Choice: Out camping for the night, the four turtles find themselves in the middle of an election. It's not any ordinary election. The two female candidates are from a distant planet where the political process is trial by combat.
Sons of the Silent Age: Taking a Huck Finn styled trip down a local river, the turtles, Casey and April discover a nuclear power plant … as well as mermen of Y'Lantias … the last of their kind.
Dragon's Brew: Hun's taking the Purple Dragons to new heights. He hijacks a top secret government shipment…one of Bishop's little surprises.

I, Monster: On a training exercise in an abandoned brick works in the boroughs, Casey Jones and our four turtles run afoul of a strange man. This is the Rat King… and even though they don't know it, the turtles have met him before.
Grudge Match: Mikey's blowing off trainings more than ever; he's the BattleNexus Champion, after all! Who needs training?

Wing and a Prayer: It's a bird! It's a plane! Okay, it's this guy with angel wings, an Avian, named Raptarr who is after this other guy with metal wings, named Mephos, who wants to take over the Avians' flying city.
Bad Day: Everything goes from bad to worse for the turtles. Life spins out of control in a nightmare of horror and pain. Who is behind all this? How will it ever end? P.S. Your cat is …

Aliens Among Us: It looks as if Agent Bishop might find himself out of a job or at least out of funding. With the President in New York City, the turtles are out watching the motorcade when they find themselves right in the middle a new alien invasion!

Capt. Marciano and Capt. Griffin struggle to regroup after colliding with Bonner Bridge; salvaging banged-up boats or hanging up their rods.
The fleet battles the elements; a greenhorn struggles to prove himself to his father; working against each other and boat misfortunes to stay afloat.
Captain Greg Mayer and his Fishin' Frenzy crew are the top earners at the start of day nine in the Outer Banks' bluefin tuna fleet.
The start of the 11th day is met with treacherous winter weather in the Outer Banks fishing grounds that forces captains to push their limits.
Family is at the forefront of fishermen's fight to fish hard and make money in North Carolina's bluefin tuna fleet.
Seven crews take on the Outer Banks hoping to catch fish that are big enough to keep; the outcome isn't looking great with the luck they've had lately.
The season is coming to an end and Reels of Fortune continues to battle Fishin' Frenzy for the top spot; all crews struggle to land fish, desperate for a paycheck.
Fleets have only five days left before the season closes; Reel Action is stuck at the dock after an accident, causing a late start for the crew and tensions onboard to reach a boiling point.
It's the final two days of the season and three Southern boats - the Fishin' Frenzy, the Reels of Fortune and the Doghouse - are each within reach of the top spot.
The fleet must overcome new obstacles yet again when bluefin season begins in the Outer Banks.

Known as the Graveyard of the Atlantic, the North Carolina coastline is littered with shipwrecks; as the bluefin season takes off, the treacherous waters claim another victim, and the Fishin' Frenzy and Hot Tuna are first on the scene.
The unpredictable waters cause more problems for boats in the Outer Banks; the captains feel the pressure as the season starts to slip away from them.
With the fishing migration in an unpredictable state, the captains resort to espionage for information, but end up with more than they bargained for.
